body.x: This vacancy announcement pertains to law enforcement and/or governmental officials within INTERPOL's member countries only.
Please read the Conditions of Secondment in force at INTERPOL (shared via the NCB) including the maximum duration of secondment.

Please be aware that your home Administration/Agency/Service/Government will be responsible for all of your salary/remuneration, social insurance, pension contributions, welfare benefits, family allowances, benefits during your assignment at INTERPOL as well as travel, removal expenses related to your arrival at and departure from INTERPOL, and any other related costs depending on your circumstances. It is requested that you obtain in writing, confirmation from your home Administration/Agency/Service/Government that it agrees with these CONDITIONS OF SECONDMENT. This confirmation letter should be forwarded to us THROUGH THE NCB.

INTERPOL is the world’s largest international police organization, with 196 member states. Created in 1923, it facilitates cross-border police co-operation, and supports and assists all organizations, authorities, and services whose mission is to prevent or combat international crime. INTERPOL is now looking for a qualified candidate as a SECONDMENT - Innovation Officer (reserve list) within the Innovation Centre which is part of the Exec. Dir. Capacity Building Innovation.
Job title: SECONDMENT - Innovation Officer (reserve list)
Reporting To: Assistant Director, Applied Innovation and Strategic Innovation

INTERPOL actively encourages applications from women and nationals of member countries that are currently unrepresented among our staff (please click on this link to access the list of countries). Candidates from these countries are particularly encouraged to apply.
INTERPOL’s recruitment process is merit-based hence all hiring decisions are made considering the applicant’s qualifications and the needs of the Organization.
INCLUDING GOALS AND OBJECTIVES OF THE POST

Within the Executive Directorate of Capacity Building and Innovation (EDCI), the Innovation Centre (IC) aims to support law enforcement agencies in understanding the rapid changes affecting policing. The Directorate facilitates knowledge exchange on how technologies impact law enforcement.

The objective is to serve as a transversal enabler for INTERPOL and its member countries, facilitating the sharing of law enforcement innovations, the identification of critical challenges, and the development of effective solutions with partners. In coordination with relevant internal directorates, the IC will support organization-wide innovation initiatives, particularly AI initiatives by contributing to the experimentation, prototyping, evaluation, and secure development of new capabilities. This includes providing a structured environment and framework for testing and validating use cases, while ensuring strict alignment with the Responsible Use of AI framework.
These efforts will be underpinned by an innovation platform that integrates the expertise of police, public and private partners, and academia.

Reporting to the Assistant Director Strategic Innovation or Applied Innovation, the post holder will help address policing challenges and operational pain points by fostering strategic partnerships, facilitating knowledge exchange, and coordinating innovation initiatives and networks to co-develop practical solutions for INTERPOL and its member countries.
The post holder will be expected to work collaboratively with colleagues within the IC and across various INTERPOL units as well as with external partners.
Serve as a primary point of contact and trusted advisor for Member Countries seeking guidance, technical assistance, and support in policing innovation.
Identify operational challenges and emerging needs, and design, develop, and coordinate innovation-driven initiatives, programmes, and projects to address them.
Promote the adoption of innovative approaches, technologies, and best practices that enhance operational effectiveness and policing capabilities.
DUTY 2: PURSUE STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIPS WITH INNOVATION ENTITIES

Monitor and assess developments across innovation ecosystems, including academia, research institutions, technology providers, industry partners, start-ups, and international organizations relevant to policing and public sector transformation.
Identify and evaluate opportunities for strategic partnerships that strengthen innovation capacity and support operational and business optimization in law enforcement.
Build and maintain strong relationships with innovation stakeholders to foster collaboration, knowledge exchange, and support for Member Countries.
Initiate and coordinate joint projects, pilot programmes, research activities, and innovation initiatives, particularly in artificial intelligence, emerging technologies, and digital transformation.
Foster a culture of innovation by promoting experimentation, continuous improvement, and the adoption of solutions that deliver tangible operational value.
Gather, analyze, and synthesize information to identify trends, opportunities, risks, and best practices relevant to Member Countries and organizational priorities.
Organize, lead, and participate in conferences, workshops, training programmes, and other professional events focused on innovation and technology-enabled transformation.
Promote the dissemination of best practices, lessons learned, research findings, and innovative approaches that enhance operational effectiveness and organizational excellence.
Identify and communicate emerging trends, technological developments, and innovation opportunities that may shape the future of policing and international law enforcement cooperation.
Perform any other duty as required by the hierarchy.

Three-to-four years’ completed University Degree or equivalent diploma, ideally with a specialization in a relevant field such as engineering, science, public policy, or law. Ten years’ experience in the area is required if the post holder does not have the required level of education. (police officer or official with equivalent expertise in criminal justice, international affairs, and/or public relations is essential).
Master's degree, or doctorate level would be an asset.

At least three years’ experience in a law enforcement organization, with a strong background in law enforcement operations and management, and a proven track record of leadership and strategic decision-making.
Demonstrated knowledge of current and emerging information and communications technologies, including practical insights into their applications and implications for law enforcement.

Specialized experience in cybercrime, financial crime, counter-terrorism, or organized crime, with a strong understanding of the legal frameworks and international agreements governing transnational investigations.
Demonstrated capability to independently plan and manage complex projects, leveraging strong problem-solving and strategic thinking skills to deliver results with minimal oversight.

Proven experience in cultivating strategic partnerships and outreach initiatives, with a successful track record of engaging stakeholders from the private sector, government bodies, and international organizations.
Proven experience in coordinating international meetings and conferences with diverse global stakeholders.
Practical experience working within innovation entities focused on business process optimization and operational efficiency.
Proficiency in a second official working language of the Organization (Arabic, French or Spanish) would be an additional asset.
Ability to align organizational strategy with unit goals, utilizing proactive thinking to develop plans that inspire and motivate staff.
Sound judgment and analytical skills to make timely, evidence-based, and bias-free decisions, supported by efficient budget management.
Excellent presentation and communication skills, with a proven capacity to build trust and foster an inclusive work environment.
Demonstrated ability to build professional partnerships with governments, international organizations, and academia within multicultural settings.
Capacity to thrive in fast-paced, demanding environments by prioritizing effectively and delivering high-quality results under tight deadlines.
Ability to engage diverse groups by adapting communication styles to ensure mutual understanding and inclusivity across cultural boundaries.
Capacity to synthesize complex information into concise, actionable formats while anticipating challenges and driving progress through creative solutions.
As part of our commitment to transparency throughout our recruitment process, INTERPOL's Staff Manual Regulation 11.4: Age-limit, which states that:

'Officials of the Organization shall not normally be retained in service beyond the age of 65 years. The Secretary General may, in exceptional cases and in the interests of the Organization, extend this age limit, in which case he shall inform the official concerned sufficiently in advance.'

Given this Regulation and in case candidates reach the age of 65 during the potential duration of the appointment, should they be selected for the position and the process proceed to appointment, the employment period may be affected by this regulatory limit and may therefore not extend for the full standard contract duration as published in the vacancy notice.
We are sharing this information to ensure transparency at this stage of the process.
This position is no longer open.
